source.title: Some common confusion about induction heads

record.tranche_reason: The post argues that mechanistic and behavioral induction heads should be distinguished and that the behavioral definition needs qualification, but does not report a direct test of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The post discusses cited results from other work, which are not rows. A comment by the author reports a REMIX finding about context-sensitive GPT2-small heads; this is recorded as a related finding that does not directly measure a listed version.
record.test_reason: Conceptual post distinguishing mechanistic and behavioral definitions of induction heads. Its only own result is a comment-reported REMIX finding: GPT2-small has context-sensitive heads that score low on the induction score. No number is given, and the finding does not measure any version's effect. The arguments on V1 (minimal mechanism, extra paths) and V3 (definition drift) rest on cited work (causal scrubbing, IOI), not the author's own results. So the post is closer to T6, discussion only, than to T5, which needs results or a specific argument from its own evidence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also says the two-head mechanism is only the minimal implementation, and that it is incomplete even in 2-layer models. He adds that behavioral induction heads generally do more than induction on natural text.
record.recipe_differences: Conceptual discussion rather than a reproduction of the original experiments; the post distinguishes definitions and discusses their limitations.
record.method_sensitivity: The author says behavior on repeated random token sequences may differ from behavior on natural text, where heads can take part in more complex context processing.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT2-small, some heads are strongly context-sensitive under causal context scrubbing but score low on the behavioral induction score. No numbers are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioral induction scores on repeated random tokens miss some heads that carry in-context processing on natural text.

record.problems: The post is primarily conceptual. The REMIX result is reported without numerical values, uncertainty, or further methodological detail in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for causal-scrubbing or IOI results cited from other work; the post does not present them as its own results.

untested.parts: Two-head composition is discussed only via cited causal-scrubbing results; there is no own test.
Argued conceptually as a definitional drift; there is no measurement of induction heads' share of in-context learning.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T6: the arguments rely on cited results, not the post's own. Because no version is tested, no labels are given. There are no instructions in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The post discusses the proposed two-head mechanism but does not report a direct test of its formation or operation.
Not addressed with a direct measurement of training timing, in-context-learning gain, or loss curve.
The reported context-sensitivity result does not measure whether induction heads account for most in-context learning or loss falling with token index in large transformers.
No cross-family, size, run, architecture, or modality test is reported.
No data or training-setup comparison is reported.
The post does not test few-shot task learning or compare its carriers.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Replaced a head's input with a modified sequence in which far-away context was scrubbed using text from a random dataset sequence; measured the resulting in-context loss increase.
rows.measure: Context sensitivity by increase in in-context loss after context scrubbing; comparison with behavioral induction-head score
rows.value: The authors report finding context-sensitive heads that score low on the behavioral induction-head measure; no number stated.
rows.locator: Comments, Alexandre Variengien reply about REMIX
rows.note: Reported in the author's comment as related evidence from REMIX. It does not measure the token-index loss behavior or the causal share of in-context learning specified by the listed versions.
rows.check: The row measures context sensitivity of heads, not induction formation, mechanism, or share of in-context learning. No value is given. It is unpublished REMIX work reported in a comment. It is correctly unlinked.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
